Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the PII mapping and a simplified data flow diagram to address #1. High-level notes below; Marcus will follow up with the KMS/subprocessor details.

- PII scope: attachment Acme_PII_Mapping_v1.xlsx maps Acme fields to our processing surface. We mark fields that touch long-term storage (S3 logs), transient KV cache (GPU KV cache), or appear only in request payloads.
- Persistence: Redwood retains inference logs for 30 days by default; logs containing customer-provided PII can be configured to purge earlier or be disabled per contract.
- Caching: GPU KV cache is in-memory per-server and does not persist to disk; we do maintain short-term request traces for debugging (configurable).
- Diagram: flow-diagram-2026.svg shows ingestion -> routing -> serving runtime (KV cache) -> optional long-term store (S3).

Attachments included: Acme_PII_Mapping_v1.xlsx, flow-diagram-2026.svg, SOC2-type2-2025.pdf (SOC2 redacted).

Next steps: Marcus will address KMS/keys and subprocessors (Q2/3). After that we can provide a final DPA with the appropriate SCC/UK addendum language.

Thanks,

Hi Emma — Marcus here from Infra Security. Answering the KMS/subprocessor specifics you requested.

1) Key management / CMK: Redwood supports two models.
   - Hosted CMK (customer-managed keys in AWS KMS): Customers can provide an AWS KMS key ARN. We encrypt long-term artifacts (S3 snapshots, audit archives) with that CMK. Keys remain in the customer's AWS account; Redwood never has the plaintext key material. See attached redwood_kms_key_management.pdf for process and required IAM policy examples.
   - Redwood-managed HSM: For customers who do not provide CMK, Redwood manages keys in an HSM-backed KMS. Access to those keys is strictly limited and logged; usage restricted to encryption/decryption for persistence operations only.

2) Subprocessors and access to plaintext PII:
   - Current subprocessors with potential access to processed data (in limited scenarios) are: Cloud storage (AWS), Monitoring & metrics (Datadog), Email delivery (SendGrid). None of these vendors have privileged access to inference runtime memory. Long-term artifacts stored in S3 are encrypted using customer CMK where configured; ingested request payloads that include PII are ephemeral in GPU memory and not written to third-party services unless explicitly configured for logging or export.
   - Controls: role-based access control, least-privilege service accounts, mandatory MFA for all access, and irreversible audit logs shipped to our secure audit store. Access to any plaintext customer data by Redwood employees requires an approved access request and is recorded.

3) SOC2 and evidence: We can provide the full SOC2 Type II report under NDA and a standard evidence pack; procurement@redwoodinference.com will send the NDA link.

4) Cross-border transfers: For EU/UK-hosted customers we support region pinning to avoid transfers. When transfers occur, we fall back to SCCs + UK Addendum and document transfer recipients in the DPA.

If you want, we can produce a short one-page annex that enumerates each subprocessor, the type of data they may see, and the mitigating controls. I attached the KMS doc and the SOC2 redacted PDF for now.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Security Lead | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
